<p class="eyebrow">OBSERVE · EXPLAIN · VERIFY</p>

## What is an LLM, and how does it produce text?

Large language models (LLMs) are a family of neural models trained on large amounts of text. Many current models use an autoregressive Transformer that predicts the next token, but LLMs are not limited to one architecture or to this single objective.

**LLM Lab connects these mechanisms to their mathematical explanations and observable behaviour.** The goal is not to trust an intuition because a diagram looks convincing: it is to understand what a component computes, verify what can be tested, and identify what remains an assumption or limitation.

</div>
::::

## Choose how to proceed

- **Understand** — Start with the [LLM panorama](llm-overview.qmd) to place model families, objectives, learning and inference.
- **Build** — Follow the [guided path](build-path.qmd) to implement a small decoder-only GPT from random initialization. **Current status:** reference inference code is tested; a complete training loop and reproducible training run are not yet available. Corpus provenance and licensing must be established before training.
- **Deepen** — Explore optional derivations and technical references, such as [tensors](tensors.qmd). These are not prerequisites for the main route.
- **Practice and experiment** — Use [exercises](exercises.qmd) and [experimental evaluation](experimental-evaluation.qmd) to test explanations against calculations and documented protocols.

Practice supports all three learning depths; it is not a fourth depth. The conceptual route and the implementation route have different orders. Their relationship is documented in the [learning path](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/learning-path.md).

## How to read a lesson

Lessons use three markers to distinguish different kinds of material:

- <span class="epistemic-badge badge-concept">Verified Concept</span> Formal definitions, equations, and explicit mathematical assumptions.
- <span class="epistemic-badge badge-code">Executable Micro-code</span> Inspectable Python/NumPy workbenches with shape invariants and assertion checks.
- <span class="epistemic-badge badge-status">Architecture / Status</span> Explicit architectural scope and roadmap milestone state.

These markers describe the evidence available; they do not make all evidence equivalent. A diagram makes a structure readable but does not prove a property; a derivation establishes a result under stated assumptions; a test checks the cases it covers; an experiment compares configurations under a documented protocol, metrics and limitations.
